jp: 明日[あした]{は|wa-topic}雨[あめ]{だって|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard it's going to rain tomorrow.
why: Passing on something you heard from someone else, after a noun, takes だって.

jp: 田中[たなか]さん{は|wa-topic}来週[らいしゅう]引[ひ]っ越[こ]す{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard Mr. Tanaka is moving next week.
why: Sentence-final って after a plain verb marks the sentence as secondhand information.

jp: 駅前[えきまえ]{に|ni-location}新[あたら]しい店[みせ]{が|ga-subject}できる{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard a new shop is going to open in front of the station.
why: The speaker is relaying news from elsewhere, so the plain form is closed with って.

jp: あの映画[えいが]{は|wa-topic}すごく面白[おもしろ]い{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: Apparently that movie is really interesting.
why: って after a plain adjective reports what others say about the movie rather than the speaker's own view.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{は|wa-topic}今日[きょう]休[やす]み{だって|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard the teacher is off today.
why: After a noun the hearsay marker is だって, passing on information the speaker was told.

jp: 山田[やまだ]さん{は|wa-topic}結婚[けっこん]した{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard Mr. Yamada got married.
why: Past plain form plus って relays news that reached the speaker secondhand.

jp: 来月[らいげつ]{から|kara-from}電車[でんしゃ]{の|no-possessive}料金[りょうきん]{が|ga-subject}上[あ]がる{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard train fares are going up from next month.
why: News heard from another source is closed with って rather than a particle that expresses the speaker's own stance.

jp: 北海道[ほっかいどう]{は|wa-topic}もう雪[ゆき]{が|ga-subject}降[ふ]った{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard it has already snowed in Hokkaido.
why: The speaker did not see the snow; って marks it as something they were told.

jp: 新[あたら]しい先生[せんせい]{は|wa-topic}とても優[やさ]しい{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I hear the new teacher is very kind.
why: A reputation passed on by others is reported with って after the plain adjective.

jp: このカフェ{の|no-possessive}ケーキ{は|wa-topic}おいしい{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: Apparently this café's cake is delicious.
why: って shows that the speaker is repeating what people say, not claiming to have tasted it.

jp: 田中[たなか]さん{は|wa-topic}風邪[かぜ]{で|de-cause}休[やす]んでいる{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard Mr. Tanaka is off with a cold.
why: Plain form plus って passes on a report of Mr. Tanaka's situation.

jp: 彼女[かのじょ]{は|wa-topic}ピアノ{が|ga-stative}上手[じょうず]{だって|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard she's good at the piano.
why: After a na-adjective stem the hearsay marker is だって.

jp: 試験[しけん]{は|wa-topic}来週[らいしゅう]{の|no-possessive}金曜日[きんようび]{だって|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard the exam is next Friday.
why: A date learned from someone else is passed on with だって after the noun.

jp: 母[はは]{が|ga-subject}今夜[こんや]{は|wa-topic}遅[おそ]くなる{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: Mom says she'll be late tonight.
why: The speaker relays a message that Mom gave, and って closes it as secondhand information.

jp: 隣[となり]{の|no-possessive}山田[やまだ]さん{は|wa-topic}来年[らいねん]留学[りゅうがく]する{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard Mr. Yamada next door is going to study abroad next year.
why: News about a neighbour that the speaker heard from others takes って.

jp: 今年[ことし]{の|no-possessive}夏[なつ]{は|wa-topic}去年[きょねん]{より|yori-comparison}暑[あつ]くなる{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard this summer is going to be hotter than last year.
why: A forecast the speaker has heard from others is reported with って.

jp: あの店[みせ]{は|wa-topic}毎週[まいしゅう]月曜日[げつようび]休[やす]み{だって|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard that shop is closed every Monday.
why: A noun predicate relayed from others takes だって.

jp: 空港[くうこう]{まで|made-until}電車[でんしゃ]{で|de-means}一時間[いちじかん]かかる{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard it takes an hour to the airport by train.
why: Information the speaker picked up from someone is closed with って after the plain verb.

jp: あの人[ひと]{は|wa-topic}有名[ゆうめい]な歌手[かしゅ]{だって|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard that person is a famous singer.
why: After the noun 歌手, だって reports what others say about the person.

jp: 電車[でんしゃ]{が|ga-subject}事故[じこ]{で|de-cause}止[と]まっている{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: Apparently the trains have stopped because of an accident.
why: The speaker heard this news and passes it on with って.

jp: 田中[たなか]さん{は|wa-topic}お酒[さけ]{が/を|potential-ga}飲[の]めない{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard Mr. Tanaka can't drink alcohol.
why: Plain negative form plus って reports a fact told to the speaker by someone else.

jp: 今日[きょう]{の|no-possessive}会議[かいぎ]{は|wa-topic}中止[ちゅうし]{だって|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard today's meeting is cancelled.
why: Announcements heard from a third person are relayed with だって after a noun.

jp: この辺[あた]り{は|wa-topic}昔[むかし]海[うみ]だった{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard this area used to be sea long ago.
why: The speaker could not have seen this, so the plain past is closed with hearsay って.

jp: 彼[かれ]{は|wa-topic}毎朝[まいあさ]五時[ごじ]{に|ni-time}起[お]きている{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard he gets up at five every morning.
why: Secondhand information about his habit is marked with って.

jp: 田中[たなか]さん{の|no-possessive}お父[とう]さん{は|wa-topic}医者[いしゃ]{だって|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard Mr. Tanaka's father is a doctor.
why: A noun predicate relayed from another person takes だって.

jp: あの公園[こうえん]{で|de-place}来月[らいげつ]お祭[まつ]り{が|ga-subject}ある{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard there's a festival in that park next month.
why: The speaker relays an event they only heard about, using って after the plain verb.

jp: 台風[たいふう]{が|ga-subject}明日[あした]{の|no-possessive}朝[あさ]{に|ni-time}来[く]る{って|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard the typhoon is arriving tomorrow morning.
why: A forecast heard from the news or others is closed with って.

jp: 来週[らいしゅう]{の|no-possessive}遠足[えんそく]{は|wa-topic}雨[あめ]{なら|nara-conditional}中止[ちゅうし]{だって|tte-hearsay}。
en: I heard next week's field trip is cancelled if it rains.
why: A rule announced by someone else is passed on with だって after the noun 中止.
